correctness.rationale: Let S be total cross transition mass, bounded by p. A trace-compression on Y-zero-sum gives mu >=1-S/q; the X-Y contrast Rayleigh bound gives mu>=(p+q)S/(pq)-1. Their minimax intersection S*=2pq/(q+2p) when q<=2p, otherwise saturated S=p. At equality, positivity of tI-P on 1-perp forces P to equal t on the Y-zero-sum eigenspace and -t on the contrast vector; these equalities make every cross row uniform and all cross row sums equal, hence every cross entry forced. In q>=2p, saturated row budgets kill all clique/internal holding weights and give uniqueness. With cross weights fixed, block diagonalization leaves eigenvalues 1, -t, +t of multiplicity q-1, and 1-qb-lambda_j(L_W); the displayed degree and eigenvalue conditions are precisely necessary/sufficient. Constructive clique weights attain all regimes and give connectivity iff p>q. Independent exact-rational numerical spectra for 48 parameter pairs corroborated attainability; finite tests do not prove global rigidity.

final_claim: For all p,q>=2 symmetric nonnegative stochastic transition matrices on K_p joined to q isolated vertices, every SLEM optimizer has uniform cross edges b=2/(q+2p) if q<2p and b=1/q if q>=2p. The optimum is q/(q+2p) or 1-p/q respectively, unique for q>=2p; for q<2p the exact feasible optimal clique weights are described by degree caps and Laplacian spectral interval.
